---
title: "Tables and files"
description: "Search the BFS tables and download any BFS file."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Many statistics are not in an API. The BFS publishes them as files: Excel
or CSV tables, PX files, PDFs, zip files, and more. You find them in the
[BFS catalog](https://www.bfs.admin.ch/bfs/en/home/statistics/catalogue.html)
with the article type "Tables". Each file has an asset number. You also see
this number at the end of the "assetdetail" URLs of the BFS website.

In this article, we search a table about students and download it.

```{r}
library(BFS)
library(dplyr)
```

## Search the tables

`bfs_get_catalog_tables()` works like `bfs_get_catalog_data()`, with the
same arguments (see [Data catalog and PXWeb datasets](pxweb.html)).

```{r}
tables <- bfs_get_catalog_tables(language = "en", extended_search = "students")
tables
```

## Download a file

```r
asset <- tables |>
  filter(title == "Students at universities and institutes of technology: Basistables") |>
  pull(number_asset)

bfs_download_asset(number_asset = asset, destfile = "students.xlsx")

readxl::read_excel("students.xlsx")
```

`bfs_download_asset()` also accepts a BFS number. If a PXWeb dataset is
too big for the API, download its PX file and read it with the pxR package:

```r
bfs_download_asset(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", destfile = "students.px")

students <- pxR::read.px("students.px") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

The PX file is in German only.

## Metadata of a file

`bfs_get_asset_metadata()` gives the metadata of a file as a nested list:
the title, the description, the publication date, the contact, the links,
and more.

```{r}
metadata <- bfs_get_asset_metadata(number_bfs = "px-x-1502040100_131", language = "en")
names(metadata)
metadata$description$titles$main
```
